species.name: Crappie
why: Water 60°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 6–14 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 55 ft, cold below.
Little oxygen below about 80 ft, so fish stay above it.

species.name: White bass
why: Water 60°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 10–14 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 55 ft, cold below.
Little oxygen below about 80 ft, so fish stay above it.
South wind at 10 mph pushes bait onto the north shore: try the wind-blown banks.

species.name: Largemouth bass
why: Water 60°F on top, much colder than they like, so they move slowly and stay deep.

The lake is layered: warm water down to about 55 ft, cold below.
Little oxygen below about 80 ft, so fish stay above it.
South wind at 10 mph pushes bait onto the north shore: try the wind-blown banks.
